articleTitle: Noise Generation in a Forward DC-to-DC Converter
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The mechanism of switching-noise generation is examined for the most popular power converter, i.e. the forward dc-to-dc converter. Particularly the output noise voltage generated during the transistor's turnoff is analyzed by dividing the turnoff time into four sequent states and deriving the corresponding high-frequency equivalent circuits. In these circuits the parameter of transistor's fall time is also introduced. As the result, not only the influence of the inductive or capacitive parasitic elements on the noise generation but also the relationship between the transistor's switching speed and the noise voltage are quantitatively clarified.

articleTitle: Current Fed and Voltage Fed Switching DC/DC Converters - Steady State and Dynamic Models their Applications in Space Technology
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This paper is a contribution in the developments. of the steady state equations and dynamic representation of current fed switching structures (buck, boost) in continuous mode. The basic principle for the mathematical modelling is the first order expansion of the transition matrices. A comparison with classical voltage fed power cells shows an higher degree in the system transmittances as the consequence of the introduction of a new system variable the input capacitance voltage. Validations are realised on a breadboard PWM shunt regulator.

articleTitle: Coupled Inductor and Integrated Magnetics Techniques in Power Electronics
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Energy storage and power processing with magnetic devices is more efficient if the separate inductors and transformers are integrated into a single magnetic structure. The origins and main results of the coupled-inductor and integrated magnetics concepts are reviewed.

articleTitle: A Selective Supervision Device for Paralleling Operating AC/DC and DC/DC Converters
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This paper describes a device suitable to control the output of several converters, each voltage regulated and parallel operating with forced load sharing, so that, when failure occurs, it becomes possible to identify and shut-down the failed unit without affecting to other parallel connected units. Undervoltage and overvoltage supervision is garanted by the device to avoid output voltage changes dangerous for the supplied equipment. The supervision device has been designed by taking in to account the use of last power transistor on the power circuit. Beacause of that, the device includes a pulse by pulse control of power transistor integrity to cut-off as possible the failed unit. Besides, the device is able to control the transistor peak collector current to shut-down the power transistor, with an automatic reset function, during output short-circuits or overloads. The device described has been utilized in the transistorized buck/boost converters and rectifiers for low power system for telecommunication plants [3].

articleTitle: Design Considerations in Multi-Output DC-DC Converter with Magnetic Amplifiers
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Multiple output dc-dc converters, that take advantage of cross-regulation, are useful power supplies for electronic equipment which require several regulated voltages with good isolation. However, since regulation errors are contained in the cross-regulated outputs, they should be stabilized to obtain a precisely regulated output. Magnetic amplifiers are suitable for this purpose, but no quantitative design method has yet been fully established. This paper proposes utilization of magnetic amplifiers to compensate for cross-regulation errors in the multi-output dc-dc converter, and describes SR optimum design conditions presenting a suitable cross-sectional area and number of turns for the SR. Further, it is also clarified that SR core can be reduced in size by utilizing an amorphous core and increasing the operating frequency.

articleTitle: Inverter Output Voltage Waveform Closed-Loop Control Technique
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Inverter output impedance which depends mainly on the AC output filter is lowered by applying a closed-loop control technique to the voltage waveform shaping. In consequence, inverter output dynamic characteristics are drastically improved; The transient voltage variation and waveform distortion are lowered. This paper explains a noble control system and shows experimental results.

articleTitle: Evolving Central-Office Powering Architectures
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This paper reviews the forces and trends that have an impact on the evolution of exchange telecommunication networks and the effect each of these may have on central-office power systems. Alternative powering architectures are discussed, with considerations highlighted for each. No prediction is made as to which of the power architectures will dominate; this will depend on the evolution of various technologies and on economics.

articleTitle: Surge Analysis of the Free-Running Transistor Inverter
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The collector current surge of the free-running transistor inverter is investigated. In this circuit, the collector current increases sharply with saturation of the core. This spike is undesirable with respect to the reliability of transistor and the efficiency. Since the generation of spike, however, brings about the commutation, we can not avoid this phenomenon. The details of its generation mechanism is unknown, so the relation between its magnitude and the constants of circuit is analyzed by using a simplified pi model of transistor.

articleTitle: Distributed Power Processing: The Systems Solution
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: A case study is described of a telecommunications system wherein the utilization of power was given serious consideration from the point of inception. The objective was to determine the power processing architecture that optimized such figures of merit as efficiency, life cycle cost, first cost and reliability without imposing any of the traditional constraints that result from initiating powering-system design after the powered-system design is complete. The two designs were considered in parallel as a total system design. The resulting system has power processing integrated both physically and functionally so that the sharp line that traditionally delineates powering-system from powered-system is not at all apparent. Paramount is the fact that every figure of merit in improved substantively over that of the less distributed, bulkier powering architectures that are common today in telecommunications systems. The use of board mounted power modules, BMPMS throughout the system provides peripheral, efficient control of power so that idle circuitry can be powered down. This is accomplished with no loss of function or perceivable delay. Simulations project that this can reduce operating electrical energy to 30 percent of what it would have been. First cost of the distributed powering scheme was significantly lower than that of traditional powering schemes. Life cycle cost is greatly reduced by the lower first cost and lower operating cost provided by distributed power processing. Reliability was very closely scrutinized by computer modeling because two effects act in opposition.

articleTitle: Centralized Supervision Systems for Power Equipment in Telephone Offices
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: NTT has developed a remote supervision system for power equipment. This system, which is installed in a power maintenance center, makes it possible to effectively supervise power equipment and to automate routine maintenance tasks in telephone offices. This system can provide access to a maximum of 32 telephone offices, monitor up to 384 alarm points and measure up to 96 points in the power equipment in each office. NTT is now promoting centralized maintenance system for power equipment in order to rationalize the power maintenance operation. Therefore, the systems have been introduced to achieve more effective maintenance in offices where there are no power maintenance personnel assigned. This paper discusses the state of the existing centralized power supervision system in NTT and the newly developed remote supervision system.

articleTitle: Improving Efficiency in Series Resonant Constant Current Converter
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Conventional constant current converters which have been employed in many transmission systems have good constant current characteristics but do not have high efficiency. A series resonant converter also has constant current characteristics and it's switching loss is small. However, the on-period loss in this converter is larger thah that for the conventional one. This paper describes a technique for decreasing on-period loss and improving the efficiency of the series resonant constant current converter. The maximum duty ratio is designed to reduce the rms current. The drive condition of the transistor is designed to minimize transistor loss, and the Litz wire is adopted as the winding method to decrease transformer and inductor losses. As a result, efficiency has been improved to 92%.

articleTitle: DC-to-AC Power Converter for Fuel Cell System
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: As the interface between fuel cells and the utility line, a self-commutated inverter is preferred to a line-commutated inverter because of its easy controllability. Using the gate turn off (GTO) thyristors, this inverter can have high efficiency and simple circuit configurations. This paper describes the design features and test results of the dc-to-ac power converter, which is principally composed of four-phase transistor chopper and 12-pulse GTO inverter, for a 50kW experimental fuel cell power system. Furthermore, new GTO inverter which improves the circuit efficiency is presented. Special emphasis is placed on a detailed analysis and evaluation of this GTO inverter.

articleTitle: Sealed Lead-Acid Battery
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: During recharge of a lead-acid battery, initially evolves oxygen gas and later hydrogen gas. These characteristics are favorable for a sealed lead-acid battery with oxygen recombination reaction. Under a limited overcharging current, no hydrogen gas evolves at the negative plate resulting in reduced polarization and lower terminal voltage. Several hundred charge-discharge cycles or about five year floating services for the sealed battery can be expected. In Japan, about twenty million cells, mainly portable smaller ones, were produced last year. Stationary sealed batteries with capacity of 30 Ah to 100 Ah have been developed.

articleTitle: A Power Feed System for Optical Data Highway Systems
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This paper describes the new power feeding system for remote terminals of an optical fiber data highway in buildings or on the premises. Our developed new power feeding system has features the following techniques to enhance reliability and design flexibility. (1) A combination of remote and local power feeding system is used. (2) This power feeding system can be applied flexibly for a larger scale system. (3) The remote power feeding system is duplicated. (4) This power supplies of the central terminal equipment(CTE) located adjacent to the computer are distributed in each functional block. (5) The remote power feeding unit contains saturable reactors operated in constrained mode, which are widely used as high reliable constant current device in submarine cable power feeding systems. (6) The remote power receiving unit contains ringing choke converter because of their simple circuit features.

articleTitle: Transient Voltage Analysis of DC Power Distribution Systems
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: An analysis is presented of voltage transients resulting from a short circuiting accident in a telecommunications DC power distribution system. Two typical sorts of DC distribution systems, bus-cable and radial-cable methods, are modeled and numerically analyzed. Main results are as follows: (1) DC distribution system models, which can simulate voltage transients waveforms accurately, are obtained. (2) A radial-cable method is desirable for limiting voltage transients. (3) Installing capacitors at a distribution board is effective to limit voltage transients.

articleTitle: High Frequency Characteristics of Amorphous Tape Wound Cores used for Controlling a Switched-Mode Power Supply
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This paper reports the high frequency characteristics of Co-rich amorphous tape wound cores under the flux resetting characteristics up to 2O0kHz. The characteristics can be utilized for magnetic amplifiers in a switched-mode power supply. The advantages of the amorphous cores have been clarified as compared with 50%Ni-Fe, 79%Ni-Fe and Mn-Zn ferrite cores. Some problems related to the stability and sensitivity of the amorphous cores are also discussed. Core noise and anomalously long transient response are the serious problems in the flux resetting characteristics. But these problems can be suppressed by increasing exciting frequency or by lowering the exciting impedance. It is found that amorphous cores are very suited for magnetic amplifiers operating at a high frequency range in a switched-mode power supply.

articleTitle: The Reliability of Auxiliary Systems - Power and Cooling; Further Insights
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This paper provides a continuation of previously presented (1) availability analysis of power and cooling subsystems in an electronic switching centre. The following items are treated in particular. Failure mechanisms of power and cooling equipment are interconnected, both subsystems including common elements such as AC power supply. Availability calculations are carried out considering this interconnection. Methods of improving the availability of air conditioning system are investigated and corresponding availability figures are derived. Conclusions are arrived at on the availability of power and cooling, treated in an integrated way.

articleTitle: A New 3kVA Standby Diesel Generating Set for use in Small Remote Telephone Exchanges
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: In the U.K. small rural telephone exchanges have invariably derived their energy from a rectified a.c. electricity supply system which is rated at a nominal 240V 50Hz single phase. The standby source of supply has been from a nominal 50V battery which could keep the equipment fully operational for at least 24 hours. The increasing use of the electronic switching systems has meant a more constant load pattern, even when the equipment is in a near-quiescent condition, and this, coupled with the need in some cases to provide a longer period of reserve power capacity, has resulted in the demand in the U.K. for a small, compact, low cost generating plant of 3kVA capacity. This paper shows how a high speed, 3000rpm diesel engine was adapted to function as part of a permanently installed generating set and goes on to explain the design features of the whole plant and its associated control system.

articleTitle: Microprocessor Control System for Large Power Plants
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: A general purpose control and monitoring system for power plants has been developed by ERICSSON, Sweden. Based on distributed microcomputers the system is implementable not only in Power Supply Plants but also in the other systems involved in generation conversion, storage and transportation of energy in conjunction with a telecommunication plant. The system has been named ERICSSON ENERGY-MASTER and is able to perform the internal control and monitoring functions for the subsystems included in a complete Telecommunication Energy Plant. The system may be used stand-alone as a Telecommunication Energy Management System with remote operation facilities or as an interfacing subsystem to a Telecommunication Network Operation and Maintenance System. This paper describes the basic structure of the system and some of its properties and applications.

articleTitle: Hybrid Power Systems for Remote Sites - Solar, Wind and Mini Diesel
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This paper describes a hybrid power supply system for remote sites, ERICSSON SUNWIND, consisting of solar, wind and mini diesel generators. As the system uses both solar and wind generators the particular advantages of this combination are discussed. A highly reliable wind generator of vertical axis type will be described. It is virtually maintenancefree and equipped with unique lightning and overspeed protections. Also it is equipped with a microprocessor-based control system for output power optimization, which will be described in another paper presented at this INTELEC Conference. The system includes two reserve energy sources, i.e. the station battery and the mini diesel generator set. The minidiesel which uses DC-generation will be described together with its control equipment. Its most important characteristics are the simple auxiliary system and the start up safety.

articleTitle: Telecommunications Power System Reliability in NTT
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Conventional reliability standards are specified by a constant value and bear no relation to the scale of the paticular power system. Today's social realities, however, dictate that the larger the system scale, the higher system reliability must be. With increasing dependence on telecommunication services in social life and consequent expansion of the telecommunications system scale, society has become dependent on consistency and reliability. Should the system malfunction, there would be significant social disruption, and a modern reliability standard must reflect the potential consequences of system failure. This paper describes a new reliability specification method for power systems which incorporates social influence.

articleTitle: A New Method for Testing Stationary Batteries Capacity in Telecommunications Systems
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: To reduce manpower required and electrical energy consumption during capacity tests on stationary batteries for telecommunications systems, a new capacity testing technique has been developed. The test consists of two steps: a short time discharge to determine the minimum capacity cell in assembled batteries and a measurement of the cell's capacity by using an automatic capacity tester. The new method and the conventional one were used in field and the results were compared with each other. As a result, large decrease in manpower required, electrical energy consumption, size and weight of capacity test equipment and measurement error was realized by using the new method.

articleTitle: Design Considerations for Power Schottky Barrier Diodes
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: (1) Theoretical equations for design of the power Schottky barrier diode(SBD) with low reverse voltage are proposed and the results of the calculation are in agreement with the experimental data. (2) These equations are applied to the optimum design for SBD with 30V-200A and good characteristics are obtained. (3) Equations for SBDs with high breakdown voltage (more than 100V) in which minority carrier injection is taken into account are proposed and the results of the calculation show agreement with some of the experimental data.

articleTitle: A Modular, Uninterruptible AC Power Plant for Telecommunication Loads
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: After a brief analysis of the power requirements of various telecommunication AC load this paper describes some different uninterruptible power plants presently adopted and compares them from the point of view of performances and reliability. It is then presented a type of uninterruptible AC power plant installed in many SIP (Italian Operating Telephone Company) exchange officies. It is characterized by high modularity and reliability, coupled to an unusually high power efficiency, taking into account the low voltage level of the DC link. The results of many years of experience with this type of equipments are reported, confirming the validity of the chosen solution.

articleTitle: Characterization and Improvement of Power MOSFET Switching Loss
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: A model to evaluate power MOSFET switching loss is developed. Frequency dependencies are measured using a one-transistor forward converter and compared with calculated ones. For comparison, maximum output powers are measured both for power MOSFETs and bipolar transistors. To reduce the switching loss and enable a faster switching a small feedback capacitance device is proposed and realized.

articleTitle: Operating Life of Aluminum Electrolytic Capacitor
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Approximately 300 aluminum electrolytic capacitors, which have been used for about 10 years in electronic switching systems, were examined to confirm any degradation by non-destructive and destructive analyses and to estimate operating life through the accelerated life test. No degradation in electrical performance, such as capacitance, dissipation factor (tan δ) and DC leakage current, was observed in non-destructive analysis before the accelerated test. Furthermore, evaporation (dry-up) of electrolyte, discoloration of separator paper and electrical chracteristics change in the electrode foil were not detected by dissection of the capacitors. Operating life for these capacitors was estimated to be sixteen years, taking into account empirical acceleration factor.

articleTitle: Battery Model using Advice Computer Simulation of PIN Diodes and RLC Circuit Topology
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The two terminal electrical behavior of batteries is simulated in detail using a circuit model based on the dynamics of the charge storage PIN diode and RLC circuit elements. The standard Bell Labs integrated circuit analysis computer program ADVICE has been used to calculate the responses shown.

articleTitle: An Improved AC Triport Without Transients in the Output Voltage
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: A new configuration of a triport system is presented. In this system, when the ac line switches to the inverter under a failure of the ac line, transients do not appear in the output voltage. The battery for the inverter is charged by the phase control of the inverter. And so there is no battery charger in this system.

articleTitle: A Three-Phase Rectifier using Energy-Constant Modulation
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This paper describes a three-phase rectifier using an energy-constant modulation technique. The rectifier with this method has three converters and is controlled by the pulse width modulation as the instantaneous energy flow through the rectifier is constant. A new control method of reducing the influence of the storage time of the switching elements is proposed. The data of the experimental rectifier are shown (AC 3ϕ 200V, DC 48V 100A, at 20KHz). In addition, the utilization factor of the switching elements is investigated and the improvement is discussed.

articleTitle: The Design of Mobile Engine Driven Generating Sets and their Role in the British Telecommunications Network
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: More than 4300 engine generating sets are installed in communications centres, forming part of the British Telecom network, and mobile generating sets in the range 5-500kW play a supporting role in relationship with their permanently installed counterparts in coping with planned maintenance or emergency situations. The paper describes the various designs which have been evolved, and the recently introduced 500kW units which are powered by gas turbines.

articleTitle: Autonomous Multi-Source Power Systems for Telecommunications
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The use of diesel powered generating sets continues to be the prime source of power for remote telecommunications applications. However, the utilisation of natural resources in the generation of power has become of widespread interest. Because of the relative unreliability of the conversion equipment and because of the lack of long term experience with it under operational conditions, the development of power supply systems that will provide the highest degree of reliability is one which uses both the available natural resources and a diesel set in complimentary modes. This paper discusses the options currently actively investigated and utilised. It also introduces applications for a low power high efficiency thermomechanical generator.

articleTitle: Reliability and Maintenance of Stationary Batteries
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: In general, lead acid batteries are prefered for telecommunication application, they attain complete recharged even at the float voltage of 2.23 V/cell. The charging process is more efficient and the voltage gap between charge and discharge is smaller compared to nickel/cadmium batteries. Several checks are discussed, which are employed to guarantee proper performance of the battery during service life.

articleTitle: Sealed Recombination Lead-Acid Cells for Standby Power
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Sealed lead-acid cells, employing gas recombination, have been specially designed for standby applications. The basic principles of design are outlined. The discharge and charge characteristics of a recombination 6V monobloc at rates varying from 5 minutes to 5 hours are given, together with data on the effect of temperature on performance. The advantages of recombination cells over traditional Planté, flat plate and tubular cells for standby applications are identified.

articleTitle: Geode-An Electrical Energy Supply with High Availability
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Project GEODE describes an electrical energy supply characterized by its very high availability. It is to be used in the PTT (French Telephone Company) telephone exchanges and is targeted for an unavailability of better than 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup>. In order to achieve this performance Merlin Gerin has adopted - a double bus bar architecture - remote controlled electrical equipment - a motor-generator set specifically designed for this project - computer assisted surveillance We present the overall reliability calculations for this project along with that for energy sources. The E.d.F (French Utility Company) network and the Motor-Generators.

articleTitle: DRO-1 A Supervision and Control Unit for Power Plants
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Increase of the operational reliability and decrease of the operational and maintenance costs for power supply plants can be realized through a continuous supervision and control of the most important functions of the power supply plant. This paper describes a supervision and control unit, called DRO-1, developed by Jutland Telephone Company. The DRO-1, which has been developed especially for supervision and control of DC power supply plants with battery back-up, is based on the know-how and the needs acquired by Jutland Telephone through many years' operation of approx. 800 power supply plants. Though the DRO-1 has been developed especially for telecommunication power supply plants it is so flexible that it will be applicable for supervision and control of other types of power supply plants with battery back-up plus control of air conditioning or energy management functions.

articleTitle: An Ultra High Speed - Large Safe Operating Area Switching Power Transistor with New Fine Emitter Structure
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The switching power supply conversion frequency has been raised annually as switching power supplies have become more compact and light. To realize high frequency power supply, circuit component frequency must also be raised and switching transistors are required to have a high-speed switching and large safe operating area. Previously, a high-speed switch was assumed to be incompatible with a large safe operating area. Scattering (S) parameters have been used to realize that this contradictory relationship can be solved by lowering base resistance. Switching transistors which have ultrahigh voltage (1200 V), high speed switching characteristics (rise time tr=200 ns, storage time tstg=2500 ns, fall time tf=70 ns), and a large safe operating area (secondary breakdown current Isb=8A, collector-emitter clamped voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">CEX</inf> (clamp) = 900 V) have been developed by using a newly devised fine emitter structure and the SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> planar structure.

articleTitle: Measurement of Quick Varying Temperature of Electrical Conductors Under Heavy Short - Circuit Excitation
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Knowledge of the evolution of the resistance of a conductor during a short - circuit allows to measure the temperature of the conductor, and makes it possible to investigate new criteria that characterize short - circuit currents.

articleTitle: High Frequency, High Power Switch Mode Rectifier, 48V, 200A, Transistor Chopping
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This design and development has been done to come up with a new generation rectifier to be used in Power Supply Plants for telephone exchanges. This new equipment will meet all Norwegian telecommunication administration (NTA) requirements and also be cost-competitive. This Power Supply module can be paralleld in an unlimit number. However, the largest power plant foreseen for NTA applications will be around 4000A. The advantages: 1) Output psophometric noise. 2) Better regulation. 3) Better transient response. 4) High efficiency ≫0,9. 5) Immediate short circuit limiting. 6) Noise back to main. 7) Power factor. 8) Less acoustic noise. 9) Easy paralleloperation with current sharing. 10) Easy service and installation. 11)Cost competitive. 12) Size W = 450 mm, D = 400 mm, H = 1800 mm. 13) Weight 120 kg. This paper will provide the users of such equipment a more detailed understanding of the features and advantages such a system has to offer. The paper also cover the main problems in the design, such as: 1) Control / Alarm. 2) HF-transformer design. 3) Mechanical design. 4) Output circuits. 5) Main circuits. 6) Switching loss and protection. 7) Driving circuits.

articleTitle: Heating and Cooling Design for a Container Hut Telephone Exchange
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This paper explains the design approach taken for heating and cooling an unmanned container hut, which contains electronic local switching equipment, to maintain the container hut air temperature and relative humidity within a given range. Electronic switch reliability is assured. A new small air-cooled package airconditioner, which has both a refrigerant cycle with a compressor and a thermosiphon in one body, was developed for this container hut. A field test clarified that the new airconditioner saves 20%~30% of the power needed for cooling, compared with a conventional airconditioner. Air temperature and relative humidity in the container hut are adequately controlled.

articleTitle: A Resonant Type Constant Current Converter with Feedback
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: A constant current converter of resonant type is presented. It is composed of the PWM control inverter, the main resonant circuit and the integrator for the feedback. The inverter being driven at high frequency, the size of the whole device can be minimized. By making use of the PWM controller and the integrator for the feedback, the output current is regulated precisely against the change of the input voltage and the loading.

articleTitle: Loss Evaluation in Converter Transformer Cores
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: A new iron loss evaluation parameter ς is presented to predict large signal iron losses in metallic and ferrite cores on the basis of the results of small signal measurements. Calculated results using ς is remarkablly in coincidence with the observed iron losses in the frequency range from several tens kHz to 1MHz. An experimental study on the relation between eddy current and hysteresis losses and tape thickness of Supermalloy cores shows that there is an economical thickness which brings about a minimum iron loss under a given frequency and flux density. This result offers an economical approach selecting metallic tape core with most optimum thickness.

articleTitle: A Low Power DC-DC Converter using a Switched-Capacitor Transformer
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: A small size DC-DC regulated converter which does not include inductance is descrived. Voltage transformation is achieved by switched capacitors, that is charging capacitors in series and discharging them in parallel or charging them in parallel and discharging them in series. In the case of inverting the polarity of output voltage, the capacitors are connected to the load as the polarity is inverted. The switched capacitors are alternately connected to the source and the load, such that the power is transmitted. Stabilization of the output voltage is achieved by controlling the period of switching `ON' of the switching elements, that is the method of EWM controlling. The DC-DC regulated converter is built in the form of a Hybrid-IC and confirmed good characteristics during the experiment.

articleTitle: Prevention of Catalyst Plug Deterioration in Lead-Acid Batteries
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Catalyst plugs, developed to obviate the need for adding water to the electrolyte in a battery, re-combine oxygen and hydrogen gases generated from the battery during float-charging to form water. This paper describes the deactivation mechanism for the catalyst (Pd-Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) and the deactivation-prevention techniques. The analysis of catalyat plugs used for several years at telephone offices has revealed that the catalyst plugs fail due to adsorption of the water onto the catalyst, and that the catalytic reaction is interfered with by the water physisorbed on the catalyst surface. A method for covering the catalyst surface with hydrophobic film was studied. Results revealed that the method reduced the amount of water physisorbed on the catalyst to one-fiftieth that on untreated catalyst.

articleTitle: The Need for and Application of Statistical Design
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: A Systematic Statistical Circuit Analysis procedure is described which uses a simple algorithm to derive the distribution of a performance parameter from the distributions and tolerances of the individual components. The procedure requires the assumption or approximation that the individual components have a normal (Gaussian) distribution, although components with other distributions can also be treated. Applications of other than normal distributions is beyond the scope of this paper. Comparisons between statistical and worst-case design methods indicate that a severe economic penalty may be encountered by designing for the unlikely worst-case, rather than allowing for a fraction of failures to occur that are negligibly small compared to the uncontrolled catastrophic failures. Two examples are shown. One derives the performance parameter from the individual component tolerances, the other determines the required component tolerances from the desired performance. Comparisons with a corresponding worst-case analysis illustrates the economic and feasibility advantages gained through the use of statistical design methods.

articleTitle: GTO Inverter for Uninterruptible Power System
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Data communication, satellite communication and other communication facilities commonly use an uninterruptible power system (UPS) for their critical AC power supplies. The requirements of the recent move toward energy conservation have led to a demand for higher efficiency in these UPS's. This paper describes the actual use the first UPS employing gate turn-off thyristors (GTO) with self-quenching functions in the DC to AC inverter main switching elements, the heart of a UPS. The UPS has such characteristics as high efficiency, higher overload capability, low audible noise and small size. First this paper describes the selection of power semi-conductor and then the new technology for the GTO inverter, and the actual applications of the UPS etc., also are explained.

articleTitle: Temperature Controlled Fast-Charge Ni-Cd Batteries
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Sealed Ni-Cd batteries have been widely used because of their excellent performance. And many fast charge system have been investigated and applied. The most popular fast-charge system is a voltage-controlled type. However the circuit is very complicated and costly. We have developed a new temperature controlled fast-charge system which are comprized of a new battery and a simple external circuit. The new batteries are designed to consume oxygen gas as early as possible and to raise its temperature as quickly as possible in the fully charged state.

articleTitle: A UPS for the Complex Communications Network
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Today's communication network requires power systems of high reliability in order to achieve the expected high performance levels of this equipment by the end users. Today's communication systems may consist of computer branch exchanges or a network connecting various communication centers around the world, carrying data, voice, or control signals. The above mentioned systems cannot tolerate power system malfunctions and still maintain signal integrity without the loss of data or process control. Many computer based Private Branch Exchanges (PBX's) cannot tolerate a power interruption of more than 1/10 or 1/20 of a second without dropping all calls in process and losing memory.

articleTitle: The Energy Policy of the French Telecommunications
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Although french Telecommunications are a rather small energy consumer, they have, as a public service, to take part in the national effort for reasonable use and care of energy. This lecture presents the stakes, goals and means of the "Telecommunications energy policy" being implemented.

articleTitle: An Advanced Li/CrOx Battery an Ideal System for Electronic Applications
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference

articleTitle: Energy Saving in Airconditioning Plants
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: An evaluation is made of the saving in airconditioning plant power in digital exchanges effected by ventilating with the cool outside air during night hours and possibly some day hours. The effect of the building insulation is also considered. This is done with the aid of a computerised programme taking into account the heat capacity of the building (total thermal time constant method). It is shown that a saving in ventilation power through the use of a special outside air unit for the conventional airconditioning cycle can be achieved. The method of analysis allows us to establish a daily or seasonal heat flow balance for a given inside temperature. The heat capacity tends to flatten the inside air temperature fluctuations. An exact knowledge of this effect makes the choice of a smaller capacity airconditioning plant possible. An additional important decrease in the size of this plant is achieved through cooling the building by nightly ventilation, making use of the heat capacity of the building.

articleTitle: Rechargeable Lithium Batteries with Copper Vanadate Positives and Mixed Organic Electrolytes
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Effects of mixed organic electrolyte on Li/Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</inf> couple were investigated. From the conductivity and Li charge-discharge efficiency, 1M LiClO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>-propylene carbonate (PC)/1,2-dimethoxyethane (DME) was selected as electrolyte. The prototype coin cells were fabricated to examine the properties of this cell system. Because of high electrolyte conductivity, the capacity at high discharge rate ( 3 mA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> ) was 450 Ah/(Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</inf> weight) Kg, which was 1.8 times larger than the capacity of the cell with 1M LiClO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> / PC alone. The cycle life also improved from 10 cycles to 55 cycles at the condition of 2e<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">=</sup>/Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</inf> depth by the use of the PC/DME compared with PC alone. Copper vanadate with mixed electrolyte seems to be a very promissing cell system for practical utilization.

articleTitle: High-Frequency Power Supply Composed of the Combination of a Thyristor Inverter and a Magnetic Frequency Multiplier
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This paper shows that the cascade connection of a thyristor inverter and a magnetic frequency multiplier produces an output power at frequency 50 kHz. In this power supply, a thyristor inverter generates 5.6 kHz square wave voltages of three phases and the nine times frequency voltage of a single phase is changed by a magnetic frequency multiplier. The multiplier is the passive device which requires nine saturated reactors with supermalloy core. We have built the 50 kHz power supply and investigated its operating characteristics.

articleTitle: An Airconditioning System using a Thermosiphon for Telecommunications Buildings
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: As heat generation per unit area from telecommunications equipment increases, equipment buildings often require extensive cooling, even in midwinter, to maintain the reference room temperature. A thermosiphon system has been developed for airconditioning in new equipment buildings. In this system, no power is required for circulating the refrigerant and the thermosiphon cooling capacity increases as the outdoor air temperature decreases. Therfore, it is expected that energy consumption for airconditioning will be greatly reduced when the thermosiphon is used for cooling in winter as well as other cool seasons. This paper describes the mechanism and characteristics of a newly developed airconditioning system employing a thermosiphon. Energy saving is also discussed for when this system is used in a telecommunications building.

articleTitle: Microprocessor Control System for Output Power Optimization of a Wind Turbine
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Another paper (1) presented at this INTELEC Conference describes a hybrid power plant for remote sites, ERICSSON SUNWIND, consisting of solar, wind and minidiesel power sources. This power plant includes a microprocessor-based control system for output power optimization of the wind turbine; - this deserves a separate description. The wind turbine used in ERICSSON SUNWIND is a combined Darrieus-Savonius type, in which the Darrieus turbine produces most of the energy, whereas Savonius rotor supplies a starting torque. The particular requirements and difficulties connected with the output power control of a Darrieus turbine are presented and analysed. In order to meet these requirements an adaptive control system based on microcomputer techniques has been developed. This paper describes the principle of operation, the hardware and the software of the control system. An illustration of the practical operation in a test plant is also given.

articleTitle: Photovoltaic Systems for Canadian Prairie Regions
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Communication industry has a need for economic low power generators for their remote sites with minimized power consumption. PhotoVoltaic generators (PV) promising hardware simplicity, low cost and low maintenance have the potential to fill this need. The operational record of PV generators is rather poor in harsh environment of the Canadian prairies. Our analysis of long term radiation data, field and laboratory tests show that often ignored cyclic winter radiation extremes and poor selection, operation and maintenance of batteries are the most frequent causes of PV system failures. We derive a reliable PV sizing curve for Edmonton (53°N, 114°W) and study various PV designs. At a cost of $20,000 per 100W a hybrid PV-TEG generator is shown to promise reliable operation which is not affected by extreme weather fluctuations of the Canadian prairies.

articleTitle: Coil & Transformer Automatic Test Equipment (ATE) System
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This paper describes the ATE System, which includes a microprocessor and is used for measuring the properties of coils and transformers. To accurately test D. U. T. with many specifications, the ATE System provides the following hardware test technologies: (1) The turn ratio measurement method, which is relatively unaffected by the transformer coupling coefficient. (2) The scanner bus line configuration, which achieved a 3-kV AC dielectric strength and 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup>-megohm insulation. (3) The winding polarity measurement method, which is relatively unaffected by transformer leakage inductance. The ATE System also provides software tests. This paper reports on the following software technologies: (1) The results of using CP/M as the operating system. (2) Using the menu system for easing operation.

articleTitle: A New Medium Power UPS using Transistor Conversion
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This paper describes a new line of utility frequency UPS designed for modern data communications and processing applications. Emphasis has been given to high reliability by the use of a simple new power switching circuit which is discussed. Very high efficiency is achieved by the use of new high voltage transistor switches which are illustrated. Problems and solutions using these switches in this application are discussed. A packaging plan which conforms with international safety standards for dead front, open door operation is shown including provision for easy front only service access. A 3Ø system with static bypass and 5th generation step PWM technology is presented with high performance characteristics. Provision for handling nonlinear loads with low distortion output is illustrated. Integration of computerized "over the telephone" diagnosis for operation and maintenance providing waveforms and an audit trail to service personnel is shown.

articleTitle: Recent Trends and Achievements in Renewable Power for Telecommunications
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference

articleTitle: Analysis of Output Voltage Waveform from Uninterruptible Power Supply Operating at a Rectifier Load
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Recently electronic communications equipment including computers and computer-related peripheral units has achieved remarkable growth and diffusion. Since this type of equipment essentially operates on DC power, a rectifier unit is generally used to convert AC power into DC. On the other hand an uninterruptible power supply (UPS) unit used for thr above equipment is designed to guarantee charateristics for a linear load, and consequently there arises a problem of output voltage waveform distortion when a distorted current peculiar to such a rectifier unit is used. In this situation this paper intends to analyze the behavior of the UPS system which is operating at a retifier load and also explain the relationship between the function of LC filter and the emergence mechanism of low harmonic distortion. A PWM inverter of new design is also introduced since it is considered suitable for disposing of rectifier loads.

articleTitle: Center-Tapped High-Frequency Inverter using ASCR
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This paper describes some transient and steady-state characteristics of a center-tapped high-frequency inverter using ASCR, which is capable of operating at 80 KHz. In the first place, the basic operation of the inverter is discussed and then the normalized numerical solution is elucidated. Effects of inductance ratio and capacitance ratio on the steady-state characteristics for the inverter are fully discussed on the basis of numerical analysis. Secondly, load characteristics and frequency characteristics attributed to load variations and frequency changes on the steady-state operation are illustrated in relation to some normalized circuit constants and operating frequency. In addition, the transient response of margin time of commutation for ASCR is studied in relation to the practical maximum operating frequency.

articleTitle: Triple Hybrid Primary Power Supply System
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Recently, various hybrid systems are proposed as primary power supplies for communications. First, hybrid conceptions are put in order. Then experiment results of the triple hybrid primary power supply system combining a wind turbine, a solar battery and a diesel generator are stated. Next, a design method for required battery capacity in various systems is given. Applying this method, the complementary grade of wind and sunshine is quantitatively observed, and it is shown that the triple hybrid system is most economical.

articleTitle: A Multiple-Output 500kHz DC-DC Converter
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The mechanism ordinarily employed for DC-DC converters consists of inverting the DC input to AC and then again inverting to a DC output. In order to miniaturize and reduce the weight of such devices, the conversion frequency must be raised to a high level. As reported below, we obtained a stable miniature DC-DC converter using a rectangular driving pulse of 500kHz and so constructed that the on-off period ratio of the output transformer is controlled by the frequency, which is synchronized with this rectangular pulse. Also, as component parts, we used power MOS FET, which was suitable for high speed switching and the low-loss transformer material 2500B2, along with large capacitance multilayer ceramic capacitors which are not subject to the problem of lifetime.

articleTitle: It's in the Air
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This paper deals with the state-of-the-art of the areas windturbines and power supply for remote telecommunications systems. The increasing reliability demands within the telecommunications industri necessitates improvement of all units in the system including the windturbine. To ensure the right development some calculation models for systemreliability must be employed. To ensure an optimal combination of windpower and back up power (hybrid configuration) an easy and quick method for determination of local windpower potential is needed. Some different windspeed distributions and their use are shown, and the influences at the local windenergy potential, from shelter, roughness of the surface, and topographical effects are discussed.

articleTitle: Current Modulation Control Method for a Multi-Output Power Supply
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Concerning a multi-output DC power supply having two or more secondary windings it was an important technical problem that the main switch would easily become a heat spot. The heat spot is predominantly caused by the power loss which occurs at the transient time. This paper describes a new circuitry and its control method that help dramatically improve the operation trajectory of the main switch and regenerate the energy stored in the main transformer's leakage inductances. Comparative measurements of the DC-DC converter section under the same conditions between a conventional multi-output power supply and the new system we developed have shown marked improvements in the reduction of peak power loss on the trajectory and of total power loss.

articleTitle: Acid Aging Behavior of Polycarbonates for Flame Retardant Plastic Containers for Central Office and UPS Lead-Acid Batteries
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: In these studies, the degradation of polycarbonates in battery acid was assessed by monitoring changes in impact resistance and melt flow rate. The effects of stress were investigated. Rates of hydrolysis were obtained from the rates of change in melt viscosity and allow estimation of service life at room conditions. These studies have shown that hydrolytic degradation of polycarbonates in battery acid results in severe reductions in strength and impact properties. These results provide a mechanistic explanation of premature stress crack failures observed in covers of polycarbonate battery containers in telephone central office reserve power usage. Potential implications of these results on the design, life and reliability of polycarbonate jars and covers for UPS* and central office stationary reserve batteries are discussed.

articleTitle: Power Distribution Supervisory Control System by Polling
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This paper describes a new Supervisory Control System (SCS) which adopts a dynamic polling structure. The need for a thinking unit at the line head for manaing a SCS is unavoidable. The thinking unit (μP) moreover, allows a communication network to be built up which uses the line without voltage, with a variable number of transmitter-receiver stations attached to the equipped centres. Configuration of the Distribution Network is discussed, the aims that the SCS must fulfil, the system functions and a digital data transmission system description.

articleTitle: Battery Charging Principles and Systems in use at the Swedish Telecommunications Administration - Present and Planned Installations
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The charging methods for stationary accumulators for use in telecommunication installations have changed through out the years. The reason for this is not only the development and the achievements in the battery technology field and the new methods and components in the control area but also the better knowledge of demands and result of the operation and maintenance work in the field. From the administrations point of view it has become necessary to find solutions which balance procuring, operation, and maintenance costs. Some of the solutions, mainly for the smaller installations, are simple and cheap, while others are quite sophisticated and hence relatively costly. The paper intends to view the development in the area concerned and to give a closer information on some of our present and future applications.

articleTitle: Automatic Monitoring DC Power Supply System
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: In this automatic power supply system, the specific gravity, level and temperature of the electrolyte are detected by newly developed sensors. The data from these sensors are analyzed, and the specific gravity and level are always displayed and the temperature is displayed in abnormal conditions. The discharge capacity at occasional discharge operation is memorized by IC installed and suitable charge capacity is provided by a charger according to the IC's content. This system has compact construction and easy maintenance due to unification of the monitor and charger.

articleTitle: Bipolar-FET Combinational Power Transistors for Power Conversion Applications
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Four Bipolar-FET combinational transistor configurations are compared from the application point of view. The configurations included are FET-Darlington (Cascade), Emitter-Open Switch (Cascode), Parallel Configurations and FET-Gated Bipolar Transistors (FGT).

articleTitle: Schottky Barrier Diode Optimization for a Low Voltage Power Converter
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Optimun barrier height and impurity concentration for a power Schottky diode for maximizing rectifying efficiency are theoretically derived. For a low output voltage, 1.5 ~ 2 V as a DC-DC converter, the barrier height has an optimum value of about 17 times the thermal voltage and the impurity concentration has approximately 1 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup>, for n-type silicon. Schottky diodes with some kinds of barrier metals, such as titanium, hafnium and zirconium were fabricated and applied to a forward mode 2 V 50 A DC-DC converter. Power loss and efficiency were investigated in comparison with control molybdenum diodes. Titanium and hafnium diodes reduced the power loss from 49 W to 37 W for main circuit total loss, which improved the efficiency from 67% to 73%, at package surface temperatures below 60°C. These diodes show better efficiency up to 85°C, compared with molybdenum diodes. Smaller heat sinks or cooling fins can be used because of those low loss characteristics.

articleTitle: New Uninterruptible Power Supply System for Satellite Communication
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This paper deals with new uninterruptible power supply (UPS) system for satellite communication, delivered to Kokusai Denshin Denwa Co., Ltd. Sophisticated operation and transfer techniques of the system consisting of two UPS units and two bypass units to improve system availability are described. Microcomputerized 150 kVA GTO UPS unit which provides excellent characteristics, waveform recording and fault diagnosis function is also introduced.

articleTitle: The J3 SCR Model Applied to Resonant Converter Simulation
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The J3 SCR model is a continuous topology computer model for the SCR. Its circuit analog and Parameter estimation procedure are uniformly applicable to popular computer aided design and analysis programs such as SPICE2 and SCEPTRE. The circuit analog is based on the intrinsic three PN junction structure of the SCR. The parameter estimation procedure requires only manufacturer's specification sheet quantities as a data base. This uniform model, denoted the J3 SCR model is shown to be a useful design aid through computer simulation of fault transients which may occur in a "Schwartz" converter. The transients simulated would not be observable without use of a highly accurate continuous topology non-linear SCR model such as the J3 SCR model.

articleTitle: Uninterruptible AC Power Supply
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference

articleTitle: Report on Triport Uninterruptible Power System - (Triport System with Transistor Inverter)
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: High power single-phase, and three-phase triport uniterruptible power systems (triport UPS) employing transistor inverters with PWM control have been developed. The advantages of the triport UPS are high efficiency, high reliability, and low cost. The transient in accordance with switching for mode change is improved. The influence of the input dc voltage variation of the inverter on the system output is reduced.

articleTitle: Characteristics of Sealed Ni-Cd Button Cells (Improved Model FT) for Computer Memory Retention
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: An improved model of sealed Ni-Cd button cells has been developed to answer diversified requirements needed when used as a backup power source to retain the semi-conductor memory in micro-computers. Its features include: (1) Improved salting-proof performance. (2) Long life at elevated temperature. (3) Lower self-discharge rate. The cells are believed to be highly reliable for use as a backup power source to be mounted on a printed circuit board for computer memory retention.

articleTitle: Preparation and Characteristic of Li14Zn(GeO4)4 Thin Films for Solid State Batteries
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Lithium conductive solid electrolyte films are expected for all solid state lithium batteries. Li<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</sub>Zn(GeO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> (LISICON) phase thin films have been prepared by r.f. sputtering and vacuum evaporation method with electron beam heating. The sputtered film surface is considerably rougher than the evaporated film surface. The conductivities of both LISICON films at 500 °C are 5 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup> Ω<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>. The conductivity of the sputtered film is higher than that of the evaporated film below 500 °C.

articleTitle: Optimum Capacity of the Ferroresonant Voltage Regulator
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Although ferroresonant voltage regulators have been used for long time, it is not clear to obtain theoretically a desirable self capacity of this equipment for a given load capacity. This paper presents the design fundamentals based on the condition of minimum self capacity. In this analysis, a resonance characteristic of basic circuit is given by the piecewise linear approximation with two segmented regions. The performance of regulator is analyzied by the use of vector analysis, and a minimum value of self capacity and quantities required for its design are obtained by this analysis using the per unit system to understand perspectively the performance of regulator.

articleTitle: Wind Generator System for Microwave Radio Relay Station
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: NTT has introduced a wind generator system at microwave relay stations. It consists of a wind turbine generator as main power source and three diesel driven generators as back up. The wind turbine generator adopts a Darrieus unit as the wind driven blades and generates 8 kW maximum power with strong winds blowing over 15 m/s. Before this introduction, NTT manufactured two different wind turbine generator prototypes, one using a propeller and the other a Darrieus unit, and field tests have been carried out since 1978. This paper describes the field tests and the wind generator system for microwave relay stations.

articleTitle: Electrochemical Characteristics of Air Electrode with Fe Phthalocyanine for Metal-Air Batteries
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: In order to fabricate the practical air electrode, the catalytic effects of iron-phthalocyanine (FePc) and FePc polymer (poly-FePc) were studied. Four methods were used to support FePc or poly-FePc on carbon; (1) Mixing, (2) Impregnating, (3) Evaporating and (4) Direct synthesizing (to synthesize poly-FePc on carbon). The polarization of electrodes became smaller in the order of no catalyst ≫ FePc (method 1) ≫ FePc (method 3) ≫ FePc (method 2) ≫ poly-FePc (method 2) ≫ poly-FePc (method 4). The electrode by method 4 (poly-FePc) kept ca.-0.2 V during 10 mA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> discharge for 230 hr, though the electrode by method 2 (poly-FePc or FePc) showed ca. 0.1 V drop during discharge. Open type Al-air cells were fabricated to examine the practical performance of the air electrodes. The cell with air electrode by method 4 (poly-FePc) showed higher voltage, compared with the cell with FePc electrode. The cell capacity was limited by formation of Al(OH)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> layer on Al electrode. From these results, the method 4 was found to be the best way to fabricate practical air electrode.

articleTitle: High-Efficiency Converter Producing Constant-Voltage Output with Constant-Current Input
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This paper describes a new constant-current input DC to DC converter, which supplies DC output voltage needed in the load, and puts back unnecessary power to the power source. In this converter, the output side consists of a constant-voltage circuit in which the impedances are variable in parallel, but its variable impedance section is provided in the alternating voltage section located between the inverter on the input side and the rectifier on the output side so that, theoretically, the serial control type constant-voltage feeder circuit without loss can be obtained by serially feeding back the controlled surplus power to the constant-current feeder circuit.

articleTitle: Development of Ultrathin Silicon and Gallium Arsenide Solar Cell for Space Application
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The ultrathin silicon (Si) solar cell and gallium arsenide (Ga As) solar cell for increasing radiation resistance and improving power to mass ratio and improving high energy conversion efficiency, have been developed from 1982. NASDA has almost completed fundemental evaluation of these solar cells and got prospect for space applications. The ultrathin 50μm Si solar cell with maximum efficiency 13.9% (average 13.2%) at Air Mass Zero (AMO) [135.3mW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> illumination and at 28°C] and the remaining Isc ratio of 82% after irradiation of lMeV electron fluences of 1 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">15</sup> e/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> have been demonstrated. While, the GaAs solar cell consists of P-AlGaAs/P-GaAs/n-GaAs and have the maximum efficiency of 19.2% (average 17.5%) at AMO and the remaining Isc ratio of 87% after irradiation of lMeV electron fluences of 1 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">15</sup> e/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: DC and AC Characteristics of Co Base Amorphous Cores for Switching Applications
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: DC and AC magnetic characteristics with Co based non-magnetostrictive amorphous (FeCo)SiB, and (Fe(CoNi))SiB ribbons in which Co is partially substituted by Ni are studied in order to apply them to high frequency cores. It is shown that the substitution of Ni for Co decreases the coercive force. H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> also depends strongly upon the thickness of ribbons, and the ribbon core with 10 μm thick shows very low values of H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> which give an applicability of cores to the Switching Regulators drived at frequencies exceeding 100 kHz. The effects of the Samarium addition on the thermal stability are shown. The addition of Sm increases the crystallization temperature and the electric resistivity. But it lowers the magnetization.

articleTitle: Transfer Mode Inverter Consisting of Uniform Pulses
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Most DC-AC inverters are apoted to control gate circuit of pulse with modulation technique, but the circuit which consists of un-uniform pulse is more complicated than this paper. This paper describes theory and more simple of circuit which is controlled by uniform pulse width modulation technique (UPWM).

articleTitle: SCR-GTO Hybrid Voltage-Clamped High-Frequency Power Inverters with Quick-Response VVVF* Control Function
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The present paper investigates a novel type of voltage-clamped VVVF high-frequency power inverter comprising fast-switching SCR's and GTO's (or Power Transistors; PTR's) which provides power regenerating and voltage-clamped effects, and its useful modified circuit versions. The state-of-the art high-frequency inverter circuits proposed herein operate stably and efficiently in the frequency range of 10 kHz to about 100kHz or more and are suitable for the large-power high-frequency switching DC-DC converters. The basic working principle of the latest prototype of voltage-clamped VVVF high-frequency inverter is described for an equivalent load model under an automatic tuned tank circuit load, and its salient features are pointed out from a practical point of view. The steady-state performances of trial SCR-GTO hybrid voltage-clamped high-frequency inverter with VVVF control function are illustrated and discussed on the basis of frequency control characteristics, external load variation characteristics and voltage regulation characteristics.

articleTitle: Taking Measures to Meet Higher Efficiency in Switching Power Supply
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This paper describes the measures of improvement in efficiency in single-ended forward switching power supply (SPS) having dimensions smaller than conventional ones, especially narrower in width. As a result, a 5V 50W SPS with 60% volume and approximately 50% weight compared to conventional SPS has been improved while increasing efficiency up to 80% with respect to the 75% efficiency of conventional SPS. Moreover, this newly improved SPS can be used for a wide range of products because it sufficiently meets the conventional SPS's characteristics.

articleTitle: Review of Cardiff Telephone Exchange Total Energy System After Three Years Operation
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: A self contained continuous power generation system as described at INTELEC 1979, was successfully commissioned and put into service in a major communications centre at Cardiff in Wales. The objective was to provide all telecommunications equipment and electrical building engineering services from a dual fuel engine-generating plant, and to recover waste heat energy to heat or cool the building. The plant, which is fully automatic, comprises five 1300kW engines using natural gas or diesel oil, and associated waste heat boiler and chiller systems. This paper reviews the functioning of the plant during its first three years of operation, and discusses the technical factors and further development of the system as experience was gained in the use of the plant.

articleTitle: Investigation on Reliability for Stationary Lead Acid Battery
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Recent requirements for the characteristics of a stationary lead acid battery have been the improvement of maintenance, volumetric and weight efficiency, as well as power characteristics responsive to usage. These characteristics should be improved without sacrificing the battery life span. This report describes the research and development undertaken to meet the above requirements and the results.

articleTitle: Power Pack Technology for NTT Digital Local Switching System
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This paper describes technologies applied to the power pack for the NTT Digital Local Switching System. To introduce a new physical design into the system, small size, low noise and maintenance free power packs have been required, aiming at setting them in each small sized equipment module, which includes many LSIs. To meet the requirement, the power pack is designed by following advanced technologies. (1) A 200kHz DC-DC converter is used in order to get a thin structure power pack. (2) A large capacitance multi-layer ceramic capacitor, which does not require periodic replacement, is applied to input and output filters in place of an aluminium electrolytic capacitor. (3) A simple filter, whose components are multi-layer ceramic capacitor and common-mode choke coil, is applied to dramatically reduce input and output noises. (4) A high performance power control IC is newly designed to decrease the number of circuit parts. The power packs are superior not only in electrical characteristics but also in equipment design flexibility, maintainability and economization.

articleTitle: State of the Art in DC-to-DC Converters
publicationTitle: INTELEC '83 - Fifth International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: A survey on the state of the arts in the dc-to-dc converter is presented. A number of important problems underlying the converter are classified into two categories, one is solvable by the averaging method and the other is not. In general, the converter circuit itself should be stable in order to reduce the size of the converter by making its switching frequency high. As examples of size reduction, we show three kinds of converter circuit techniques in which magnetics plays a key role. The first deals with a high frequency magnetic amplifier to suppress the current surge in high speed switching, the second with a ferro-resonant circuit driven by a high frequency inverter and the third with a high frequency converter of megahertz order which is based on a multi-vibrator. In these examples, we show that the amorphous core is effectively used for magnetic components.

articleTitle: Power System of New International Switching Center of KDD
